suggestions.assertion: Does NOT spawn citation-analyst for a widely-known standard fact — avoids wasting agent overhead on trivial queries
suggestions.reason: This expectation cannot be fairly evaluated in an eval harness where the Task tool is unavailable. The citation-analyst was absent due to infrastructure constraints, not skill logic. To properly test this expectation, the eval must run in an environment where the Task tool is callable so we can observe whether the skill conditionally skips it for simple queries. As written, this expectation will always appear to pass (trivially) in the current harness — which is misleading because the skill may actually always spawn citation-analyst unconditionally.

No assertion checks whether the report's answer is factually correct (i.e., that HTTP 404 actually means 'Not Found' / resource not found). The report could pass all current assertions even if it gave a wrong definition. Consider adding: 'The report states that 404 means the server cannot find the requested resource (Not Found)' — a minimal correctness check.

The 'directly answers' expectation (assertion 3) is somewhat weak: any report with an Executive Summary section technically satisfies it. A stronger version would check that the answer appears within the first 2-3 sentences of the output, not buried after methodology.

eval_feedback.overall: The eval captures proportionality well (worker count, bibliography size, report length). The main gap is that expectation 4 is untestable in this harness — the tool was unavailable, so silence is not evidence of correct skill behavior. The eval also lacks a correctness assertion for the actual answer content.
